definitions.explanation: A party or gathering held to welcome a new member, colleague, or guest. Composed of 歓迎 (welcome) + 会 (gathering). Very common in Japanese workplace and school culture.

examples.japanese: {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}の{歓迎会|かんげいかい}を{開|ひら}く。
examples.english: We're holding a welcome party for the new employees.

examples.japanese: {歓迎会|かんげいかい}の{幹事|かんじ}を{任|まか}された。
examples.english: I was put in charge of organizing the welcome party.

examples.japanese: {留学生|りゅうがくせい}のための{歓迎会|かんげいかい}では、{自己紹介|じこしょうかい}の{時間|じかん}が{設|もう}けられていた。
examples.english: At the welcome party for exchange students, time was set aside for self-introductions.

notes:
USAGE:
{歓迎会|かんげいかい} is a fixture of Japanese organizational culture. Companies, schools, and clubs regularly hold them when new members join, especially in April at the start of the fiscal and academic year. They are often combined with {送別会|そうべつかい} (farewell party) as {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歓迎会|かんげいかい}を{開|ひら}く (hold a welcome party)
- {歓迎会|かんげいかい}の{幹事|かんじ} (party organizer)
- {歓迎会|かんげいかい}に{出席|しゅっせき}する (attend a welcome party)
- {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい} (combined welcome and farewell party)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{送別会|そうべつかい} is a farewell party for someone leaving. {懇親会|こんしんかい} is a social mixer or get-together, broader than a welcome event.
